extracted.intended_audience: Users of the SINGULAR computer algebra system (mathematicians / computational algebraists) who need to call library procedures for homological algebra, normalization, modular algorithms, integer programming, and monomial-ideal operations.
extracted.subtask_description: Reference documentation for SINGULAR library procedures: describes usage, assumptions, return values, options, and examples for functions in homolog.lib, integralbasis.lib, intprog.lib, locnormal/modnormal/modstd libraries, and monomialideal.lib.

rubrics_metrics.name: homology
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: homology(A,B,M,N); Compute a presentation of ker(B)/im(A) where M,N are submodules presenting M'=R^m/M and N'=R^n/N and A,B induce maps R^k -> R^m -> R^n.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Return: module H, a presentation of ker(B)/im(A). Note: If ker(B)=im(A) homology returns a free module of rank m. Examples show how to call with modules/matrices and how to get dimensions via dim(H) and vdim(H). The procedure assumes basering is set and inputs present modules appropriately. The result should be std()-ed for canonical presentation in examples.

rubrics_metrics.name: isCM
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: isCM(M); Test whether M' = coker(M) is Cohen-Macaulay (returns 1) or not (returns 0).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assume: basering is local. Return: 1 if Cohen-Macaulay, else 0. Examples demonstrate calls on modules; output is 0 or 1. Use to quickly check Cohen-Macaulay property of quotient by module presentation.

rubrics_metrics.name: isFlat
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: isFlat(M); Returns 1 if M' = coker(M) is flat, 0 otherwise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples show testing coker(M) over different quotient rings (qring fetch) to determine flatness over various base rings. The procedure returns 0/1 indicating flatness; use fetch/setring to change context and test across rings. Comments remark whether coker(M) is flat over the given ring.

rubrics_metrics.name: isLocallyFree
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: isLocallyFree(M,r); Returns 1 if M' = coker(M) is locally free of constant rank r, else 0.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assume: M module and r integer rank. Example uses fitting ideal and qring to check locally free of rk 1 as R/I-module. Return 1/0. Use when testing if presentation yields a vector bundle / projective module of given constant rank over quotient.

rubrics_metrics.name: isReg
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: isReg(I,M); I ideal, M module. Return 1 if given (ordered) list of generators for I is a coker(M)-sequence, else 0.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notes/examples: demonstrates independence from generator ordering (result independent of sorting) and testing in local rings. Use to check whether a sequence is regular with respect to coker(M). Returns 1/0.

rubrics_metrics.name: hom_kernel
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: hom_kernel(A,M,N); Compute a presentation K of ker(A') where A': coker(M) -> coker(N) is induced by matrix A.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compute: given submodules M,N presenting M',N' and matrix A:R^m->R^n inducing A', hom_kernel computes module K presenting ker(A'). Return: module K. Examples show computing dim(std(K)) and vdim(std(K)), and printing K. Use when one needs explicit presentation of kernel of induced map on cokernels.

rubrics_metrics.name: kohom
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: kohom(A,k); Returns matrix representing Hom(R^k, A) given matrix A defining map F1 -> F2 of free R-modules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Return: matrix of Hom(R^k,F1) -> Hom(R^k,F2). Example prints an expanded block matrix. Use for building Hom-maps on multiple copies (tensoring with free module of rank k). Inputs: A matrix and integer k.

rubrics_metrics.name: kontrahom
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: kontrahom(A,k); Returns matrix representing Hom(A,R^k) given matrix A defining map F1 -> F2 of free R-modules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Return: matrix of Hom(F2,R^k) -> Hom(F1,R^k). Example shows block-structured matrix output. Use to compute dual-Hom matrices into free rank-k module. Inputs: matrix A and integer k.

rubrics_metrics.name: KoszulHomology
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: KoszulHomology(ideal_f, M, p); Compute a presentation of the p-th Koszul homology H_p(f1,...,fk; M') where M' = coker(M) and f1..fk are generators of the input ideal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Return: module H such that coker(H) = H_p(...). Note: computed presentation is minimized via prune; if homology is 0 then returns 0. Input ideal size must be <= 20. Examples show calls for p=0,1,2 and outputs of generators. Use to compute Koszul homology modules for small generator lists.

rubrics_metrics.name: tensorMod
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: tensorMod(M,N); Compute a presentation matrix A for the tensor product T = coker(M) tensor coker(N).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compute: if M: R^r -> R^s and N: R^p -> R^q then A defines R^(sp+rq) -> R^(sq) -> T -> 0 with coker(A) = tensorprod(coker(M), coker(N)). Return: matrix A. Example prints explicit block matrix. Use to obtain presentation of tensor product of modules represented by presentation matrices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tor
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: Tor(v, M, N [, thirdArg]); Compute a presentation of Tor_k(M',N') for k specified by v (int or intvec), where M' = coker(M), N' = coker(N).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Return: if v is int -> module Tor for that k; if intvec -> list of modules for each k; if thirdArg provided -> list with Tor modules, their SB, and matrices representing k-bases. Display controlled by printlevel: >=0 shows affine dimension of Tor_k (default); >=1 shows matrices Ak,Ak+1 and kbase (if finite dim). Notes explain algorithm (using resolutions and tensor complexes) and give examples for different printlevel settings. Use Tor(k,syz(M),syz(N)) or prepare resolutions using mres and call Tor with those.

rubrics_metrics.name: integralBasis
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: integralBasis(f, intVar [, options]); Compute an integral basis of the integral closure of k[x] in k(x,y) given irreducible polynomial f in two variables (monic in the intVar-th variable).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Return: list l where l[1] is an ideal I and l[2] is polynomial D such that basis elements are I[i]/D. Options: "global" (compute normalization globally) or "local" (default: compute in localization at each singular component), "isIrred" (assume f irreducible), list("inputJ",ideal) or list("inputC",ideal) for advanced use (may produce wrong result if misused). Theory: computes normalization and converts module generators to k[x]-basis. Example shows returning basis elements and denominator. See also normal library.

rubrics_metrics.name: solve_IP
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: solve_IP(A,bx,c,alg [, prsv]); Solve integer programming problem(s) using Groebner-basis-based algorithms. A intmat, bx intvec or list, c intvec, alg string (algorithm code), optional prsv intvec for algorithms needing positive row-space vector.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Return: solution(s) of IP problem(s) same type as bx or message 'not solvable'. Supported alg codes: ct, pct, ect, pt, blr, hs, du. 'ct' and 'pct' allow computing optimal solution directly from right-hand vector b (pct requires nonnegative A,b). Other algorithms require initial feasible solution(s). 'blr' and 'hs' need a positive vector in row space of A or supply prsv. bx can be a list of right-hand vectors or initial solutions. Examples illustrate different call forms and error messages when requirements unmet. See referenced sections for theory (Toric ideals and integer programming).

rubrics_metrics.name: locNormal
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: locNormal(I [, options]); Compute normalization of affine domain R/I using local-to-global algorithm; I prime ideal (algorithm also works for radical ideals unless normal detects non-prime).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Options: modular (use modular approach with increasing primes), noVerification (if modular used, do not verify), returns list [U,d] where U ideal and d universal denominator such that U/d is normalization (returned as ideal and polynomial of base ring). Remarks: algorithm stratifies singular locus, applies local normalization at strata and assembles results; modular option returns probabilistic or verified result depending on noVerification. Example shows typical call. See references cited for algorithmic details.

rubrics_metrics.name: modNormal
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: modNormal(I, n [, options]); Compute normalization using modular methods (apply normalization over finite fields and lift results). I prime ideal (works for radical ideals unless normal command detects non-prime), n positive integer number of primes to use at a time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Options: noVerification, printTimings, int ncores (default 1). Return: list [U,d] with U ideal and d universal denominator such that U/d is normalization. Remarks: uses modular lifting (Chinese remainder + rational reconstruction) until lifted result is correct modulo an additional prime; probabilistic unless verification requested. Example illustrates usage with noVerification. See references for theory and implementation details.

rubrics_metrics.name: modStd
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: modStd(I [, exactness]); Compute a standard (Groebner) basis of I over rationals using modular methods. exactness int: 1 (default) ensures exact result, 0 gives high-probability result.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Return: a standard basis of I. Examples show behavior on homogenized ideals and use of exactness=0 for probabilistic result. Use when computing Groebner bases over Q with modular acceleration; exactness controls whether final verification to guarantee correctness is performed.

rubrics_metrics.name: modSyz
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: modSyz(I); Compute syzygy module of ideal/module I over rationals using modular methods (high probability).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Return: generating set of syzygies. Note: syzygy property is tested. Example shows returned syzygies and simplify(syz(I),1) for simplification. Use when syzygies over Q required with modular speedup; results are probabilistic but checked.

rubrics_metrics.name: modIntersect
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: modIntersect(I,J); Compute generating set of intersection of ideals/modules I and J over rationals using modular methods (high probability).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Return: generating set of intersection (minimal monomial generating set when applicable). No additional tests performed. Example shows result. Use to compute intersections over Q efficiently; output is probabilistic.

rubrics_metrics.name: isMonomial
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: isMonomial(I); Test whether ideal I is monomial. Returns 1 if monomial ideal, else 0.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assume: I ideal of base ring. Return: 1/0. Examples demonstrate mixtures of monomial and non-monomial generators and the result. Useful as a guard before calling monomial-specific procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: minbaseMon
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: minbaseMon(I); Return minimal monomial generators of monomial ideal I (returns -1 if generators of I are not monomials).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assume: I generated by list of monomials. Return: ideal of minimal monomial generators. Example shows returned minimal generators. Use to canonicalize monomial generating set.

rubrics_metrics.name: gcdMon
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: gcdMon(f,g); Return greatest common divisor monomial of monomials f and g.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assume: f and g are monomials. Return: monomial gcd. Example given. Use in monomial arithmetic and divisibility checks.

rubrics_metrics.name: lcmMon
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: lcmMon(f,g); Return least common multiple monomial of monomials f and g.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assume: f and g are monomials. Return: monomial lcm. Example given. Use in combinatorial monomial ideal operations.

rubrics_metrics.name: membershipMon
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: membershipMon(f,I); Test membership of polynomial f in monomial ideal I. Returns 1 if f in I, 0 if not, -1 if I,f nonzero and I not monomial.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assume: I is a monomial ideal. Return: 1/0 or -1 for precondition failure. Examples show positive and negative membership tests. Use to quickly decide membership without full Groebner computation when ideal is monomial.

rubrics_metrics.name: intersectMon
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: intersectMon(I,J); Return intersection of monomial ideals I and J (returns -1 if inputs not monomial ideals).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assume: I,J monomial ideals. Return: minimal monomial generating set of intersection. Example shows returned list of generators. Use for fast intersection computations specialized to monomial ideals.

rubrics_metrics.name: quotientMon
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: quotientMon(I,J); Compute quotient ideal I:J for monomial ideals I and J (returns -1 if inputs not monomial).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assume: I,J monomial ideals. Return: minimal monomial generating set of quotient. Example lists returned generators. Use for monomial ideal quotient computations avoiding Groebner machinery.

rubrics_metrics.name: radicalMon
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: radicalMon(I); Compute radical of monomial ideal I (returns -1 if I not monomial).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assume: I monomial ideal. Return: minimal monomial generating set of radical. Example demonstrates output. Use for fast radical computation in monomial case.

rubrics_metrics.name: isprimeMon
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: isprimeMon(I); Test whether monomial ideal I is prime. Returns 1 if prime, 0 if not, -1 if I not monomial.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assume: I monomial ideal. Return 1/0/-1. Examples show prime and non-prime outcomes. Use as a quick primality test specialized for monomial ideals.

rubrics_metrics.name: isprimaryMon
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: isprimaryMon(I); Test whether monomial ideal I is primary. Returns 1 if primary, 0 otherwise (returns -1 if I not monomial).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assume: I monomial ideal. Return 1/0/-1. Example placeholder shown in manual. Use to detect primary monomial ideals efficiently.
